roleTitle: Product Requirements Analyst, Collaboration Software Subscriptions
jobDescription: The subscription product team of a collaboration-software vendor builds the self-service billing and seat-management pages for business customers. The Product Requirements Analyst gathers requirements from subscription operations and customer success, writes user stories and acceptance criteria, runs acceptance testing, and is expected to show that delivered self-service features reduce billing support tickets, measured against the team's recorded monthly baseline.
requirements: Turns requests from subscription operations and customer success into user stories, each with acceptance criteria.
Leads acceptance sessions for the self-service billing pages and logs what passed and what failed.
Shows that delivered self-service features reduce billing support tickets, measured against the recorded monthly baseline.
Agrees release scope with engineering and subscription operations and keeps a record of who decided what.
Publishes release notes covering limitations and what the support team needs to take over.

evidence.text: Turned the weekly intake from subscription operations and customer success into user stories for the self-service seat-change and invoice-download pages, each story carrying its acceptance criteria.
Led acceptance sessions for three billing-page releases with two operations analysts and a customer success manager, logging every criterion as passed or failed.
Agreed release scope in sprint planning with the engineering manager and the subscription operations lead; scope and the release date were the engineering manager's call.

Published release notes for the seat-change and invoice-download pages that spelled out one limitation (invoices older than twelve months could not be downloaded) and what the support team needed to take over.
Two years on the subscription product team covering intake, story writing, acceptance sessions and release notes for the self-service billing pages.

Work sample: the story set for the invoice-download page with its acceptance criteria, plus the pass/fail log from one acceptance session; ticket identifiers are included so the entries can be traced.

Recruiter screen: candidate said billing tickets 'fell by about 30 percent' after the invoice-download page launched; he said the support team had mentioned it in a stand-up and that he had not seen a ticket report himself.
Hiring manager pre-read: the support director has asked whether this candidate has reduced ticket volume before; please make the packet explicit about which reductions are documented.

propositions.text: The candidate gathered requirements from subscription operations and customer success and wrote the user stories and acceptance criteria for the seat-change and invoice-download pages.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the stories and criteria.

propositions.text: The candidate ran acceptance testing for three releases of the billing pages and recorded outcomes in the test log.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the test log document the acceptance testing.

propositions.text: The invoice-download page the candidate specified reduced billing support tickets by 30 percent.
propositions.rationale: The figure is a stand-up remark relayed by the candidate; no ticket report, baseline or period is in the materials.

gold.expectedGap: No ticket report in the materials measures billing support tickets before and after the invoice-download page launched.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the stand-up figure out of the evidence; the materials document the stories, the tests and the releases, not a measured change in ticket volume.
followUpTargets: Ask for the monthly billing-ticket report with the baseline and the launch date of the invoice-download page.
